00:04.000–00:05.000: A male voice begins speaking. The voice is clear, mid-range, with a slight reverb suggesting a recording in a medium-sized room. He says: “Why don’t I see Nirvana right now?”

00:05.000–00:06.000: The male voice continues, same tone and quality: “You do not see Nirvana right now because you imagine a seer and a world, and neither is there.”

00:06.000–00:07.000: The male voice continues: “What is called manana is the imagining in egoistic terms, imparting reality to illusory things.”

00:07.000–00:08.000: The male voice continues: “Only a looking is there, nothing worth looking at.”

00:08.000–00:09.000: The male voice continues: “Only a seeing is there, nothing to be seen.”

00:09.000–00:10.000: The male voice continues: “The law of dependent arising is already implicated.”

00:10.000–00:11.000: The male voice continues: “There is therefore no seer apart from the phenomenon of seeing, according to the Tathagata.”

00:11.000–00:12.000: The male voice continues: “Samsara is a whirlpool as far as the ordinary beings caught up in it are concerned.”

00:12.000–00:13.000: The male voice continues: “Now what about the arhants?”

00:13.000–00:14.000: The male voice continues: “How is the idea of this whirlpool presented in the case of the arhants?”

00:14.000–00:15.000: The male voice continues: “It is simply said that for them there is no whirling round for there to be a designation.”

00:15.000–00:16.000: The male voice continues: “Pattam te sam natti panna panaya.”

00:16.000–00:17.000: The male voice continues: “So in their case, there is no whirling round to justify a designation.”

00:17.000–00:18.000: The male voice continues: “This then is something deeper than the whirlpool itself.”

00:18.000–00:19.000: The male voice continues: “The whirlpool can be pointed out because of its activity, but not so easily the emancipated ones.”

00:03.500 --> 00:06.000: A male voice begins speaking. “What keeps it going?” — clear, mid-range, natural timbre, moderate pace. No background noise.

00:06.000 --> 00:07.000: The first voice ends. Silence.

00:07.000 --> 00:10.000: A second male voice begins. “Thirst keeps it going, impelled by that making it into something, it runs towards the mirage, the gap is ignored.” — slightly lower pitch, deliberate pacing, clear diction.

00:10.000 --> 00:11.000: The second voice ends. Silence.

00:11.000 --> 00:14.000: A third male voice begins. “What impels one to ignore that gap is thirst.” — similar pitch and tone to the second, slightly more resonant, measured delivery.

00:14.000 --> 00:15.000: The third voice ends. Silence.

00:15.000 --> 00:18.000: A fourth male voice begins. “Perception. What impels one to ignore that gap is craving.” — slightly higher pitch than previous, more emphatic on “craving,” clear articulation.

00:18.000 --> 00:19.000: The fourth voice ends. Silence.

00:19.000 --> 00:22.000: A fifth male voice begins. “That desire, that lust, that delight, that craving in form, feeling, perception, preparations, consciousness, which which one is attached and thoroughly attached to it, therefore is one called a being.” — slower, more deliberate, with slight pauses between phrases, slightly lower pitch.

00:22.000 --> 00:23.000: The fifth voice ends. Silence.

00:23.000 --> 00:26.000: A sixth male voice begins. “In this way we can understand the difference between the two words papancha and pamada in respect of the nuances associated with them.” — clear, academic tone, steady pace.

00:26.000 --> 00:27.000: The sixth voice ends. Silence.

00:27.000 --> 00:30.000: A seventh male voice begins. “Commentaries very often explain the term papancha simply as a synonym of craving, conceit and views.” — slightly faster pace, more clipped articulation.

00:30.000 --> 00:31.000: The seventh voice ends. Silence.

00:31.000 --> 00:34.000: An eighth male voice begins. “Tanha, ditti, mana, nyan, etam adi vachanam.” — recites Pali phrase with clear enunciation, slightly elevated pitch on “etam,” then lowers.

00:00:03.000 --> 00:00:04.000: A male voice begins speaking. “How is the sense of self constructed?”

00:00:04.000 --> 00:00:05.000: The male voice continues. “The sense of self is constructed like this: when one looks into a mirror, one suddenly becomes self-conscious.”

00:00:05.000 --> 00:00:06.000: The male voice continues. “Even with no such notion, the moment one looks, one is reminded of it, as if to exclaim, ‘Ah, here I am.’”

00:00:06.000 --> 00:00:07.000: The male voice continues. “Even if one already has no such notion, the moment one looks into a mirror, one is suddenly reminded of it, as if to exclaim, ‘Ah, here I am.’”

00:00:07.000 --> 00:00:08.000: The male voice continues. “This is the gist of what Ven. Punnamantani Putta is trying to put across through this discourse.”

00:00:08.000 --> 00:00:09.000: The male voice continues. “This shows that the conceit ‘I’ arises due to the five grasping groups.”

00:00:09.000 --> 00:00:10.000: The male voice continues. “The gist of this paragraph is that the non-manifestative consciousness, which is infinite and all-lustrous, is free from the qualities associated with any of the concepts in the list, such as the earthiness of earth and the wateriness of water.”

00:00:10.000 --> 00:00:11.000: The male voice continues. “That is to say, it is not under the influence, it does not partake of them, ‘anubhutam.’”

00:00:11.000 --> 00:00:12.000: The male voice continues. “Whatever nature the word attributes to these concepts, whatever reality they invest it with, that is not registered in this non-manifestative consciousness.”

00:00:12.000 --> 00:00:13.000: The male voice continues. “That is why this consciousness is said to be uninfluenced by them.”
